Kolbiel Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kołbiel, Poland

Demolished. Jews began settling in Kołbiel at the end of the 18th century; by 1909, 2,077 Jews made up 89% of the village's population, though by 1921 that had fallen to 1,130 (65.3%), most murdered at Treblinka in September 1942. The cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though correspondence confirms it existed by 1853, and burial-registration delays referenced in that correspondence suggest it operated even earlier. During WWII the Germans carried out executions here - a family of eight shot in January 1943, five more in December 1943 - and in 1944 the Red Army used the grounds as a bridgehead. Tombstones were later repurposed for construction and reinforcing ditches and bridges; only three damaged stelae and about 20 fragments survive.
